policy_presence.summary: Yale University distributes generative AI governance across course-level instructor authority, GSAS personal conduct standards, and Provost guidelines.

coursework.summary: Instructors specify permitted AI use in course syllabi. Students must not use AI tools in coursework or evaluations unless explicitly authorized.

exams.summary: Permissibility of generative AI during exams is determined by individual instructors in course policies and syllabi; AI use is not permitted unless authorized by the instructor. There is no university-wide blanket permission or mandatory in-writing format unless specified in the course syllabus.

ai_disclosure.summary: Under GSAS academic integrity standards, students must attribute all AI assistance and possess the ability to articulate their research and composition process, including draft history if requested.

privacy_data_entry.summary: Yale's September 2023 Provost guidance prohibits entering confidential, legally restricted, or proprietary data into external AI tools. Enterprise services (such as Clarity, Copilot, and Claude Enterprise) operate under institutional agreements, but Clarity Radiate web search transmits queries externally and is restricted to Low Risk data. ePHI and DUA-governed data are restricted.

academic_integrity.summary: Inserting AI-generated content into submitted work without proper attribution constitutes an academic integrity violation. Under GSAS 2026–2027 standards, graduate students must consult relevant faculty before using AI in coursework or research and must be prepared to articulate and demonstrate their drafting process if requested, but there is no universal requirement for all students to log every prompt. Disciplinary responses are managed by the Committee on Regulations and Discipline; written student statements are ordinarily due within two weeks.

approved_tools.summary: Yale provides institutional tools including Microsoft Copilot, Clarity, and Claude Enterprise, and permits Zoom AI Companion with account controls. Tool availability does not confer academic assessment permission.

named_ai_services.summary: Yale provides institutional tools including Microsoft Copilot, Clarity, and Claude Enterprise, and permits Zoom AI Companion with account controls. Tool availability does not confer academic assessment permission.

teaching_guidance.summary: Yale Poorvu Center and Provost office offer pedagogy and syllabus recommendations for faculty.

research_guidance.summary: Yale Library guidance requires that use of generative AI with licensed electronic resources must comply with vendor license agreements, which often prohibit commercial text and data mining or feeding content into external AI models.
